clues: This frontier town is in the far west of Tanzania in East Africa. It sits about 500 kilometres north of Mbeya.
All the roads into town are still unsealed dirt roads. At the height of the wet season, in February and March, they can be impassable for brief periods.
In 2012, the Katavi Region was carved out of the old Rukwa Region. This town was made its main office centre.
Park rangers run their main office from a spot just south of town. Their wild park is best known for its hippos.
The town's fine cathedral is known for its grand picture windows. It became the heart of a new diocese in October 2000.
